synthesis: Nothing reached 'read' today. Skim Diffusion Tree Sampling, which brings search-style inference-time adaptation to crystal generative models, and the PXRD-guided sequential molecular CSP paper. The landmark pick, MatterGen (A generative model for inorganic materials design), is the one worth a careful read.

landmark.title: A generative model for inorganic materials design
landmark.abstract: Abstract The design of functional materials with desired properties is essential in driving technological advances in areas such as energy storage, catalysis and carbon capture 1–3 . Generative models accelerate materials design by directly generating new materials given desired property constraints, but current methods have a low success rate in proposing stable crystals or can satisfy only a limited set of property constraints 4–11 . Here we present MatterGen, a model that generates stable, diverse inorganic materials across the periodic table and can further be fine-tuned to steer the gener
landmark.seed_title: A generative model for inorganic materials design
landmark.worth_30_min: MatterGen is a landmark paper. It is a diffusion model that generates whole periodic crystals by jointly denoising atom types, fractional coordinates and the lattice. Compared with earlier generative models, it produced many more stable, novel structures that sit close to DFT local minima. It also introduced property-conditioned generation through fine-tuned adapters, with experimental synthesis as validation. It turned generative design into a credible alternative to search.
landmark.inspiration: For MCSP, it suggests replacing or seeding GA initial pools (the Genarris role) with a diffusion prior over molecular packings. Learned denoising moves could serve as GA mutations, and classifier-free guidance could steer toward a target space group, density or Z'. Generated candidates would still be ranked by dispersion-corrected DFT. It also prompts a question: can generative priors cover polymorph landscapes better than random or symmetry-constrained sampling?
landmark.foundations: Score-based diffusion on non-Euclidean, periodic domains: wrapped-normal noise on fractional coordinates (a torus), discrete diffusion for atom types, and a lattice noise schedule that keeps symmetry in mind. Equivariant/invariant graph denoisers for crystals. Classifier-free guidance and adapter fine-tuning for conditioning. Evaluation via stability relative to a convex hull, novelty/uniqueness via structure matching, and DFT relaxation distance.
landmark.reading_guide: About 5 min: abstract plus Fig. 1 (the corruption process for each variable, plus conditioning). About 10 min: Methods on periodic coordinate diffusion, lattice diffusion and the adapter/guidance scheme. About 10 min: the stability/novelty comparison figures against earlier generative baselines, and the RMSD-to-relaxed-structure results. About 5 min: the experimental synthesis case. Skip the per-property application details and the long supplementary benchmarks.

items.title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
items.abstract: Diffusion-based generative models have become strong priors over plausible crystal structures, but turning that prior into promising candidates requires steering toward several conflicting properties at once. Fine-tuning is expensive and produces a new model for every new objective, while differentiable guidance is not applicable to many real-world tasks. We instead adapt these generative models at inference time using Diffusion Tree Sampling (DTS), a Monte Carlo tree search procedure over the denoising trajectory. We make two technical contributions on top of DTS that are particularly relevant for AI-for-science applications. First, we show how to use existing property-conditional generative models (e.g., models fine-tuned for classifier-free guidance) as guided proposals inside DTS, without distorting the target distribution. Second, we extend DTS to multi-objective sampling, so that a single search produces samples spanning an entire Pareto front. We instantiate both adaptations on de novo crystal generation: improving the stability of crystals generated by different models, using pretrained conditional models to generate crystals belonging to rare space groups or with high bulk

items.title: Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms
items.abstract: Generative models play a rapidly growing role in the design and simulation of molecules. The most widely used applications of generative models are in large language models (LLMs), owing to the natural flexibility of language for specifying and answering queries. However, generalist LLMs do not effectively handle large sets of 3D coordinates, whereas specialist generative models of 3D molecules cannot reach the controllability afforded by language. To bridge these capabilities, we propose Nahual, a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion model for any sequence of text and 3D molecules. To enable expressive autoregression on continuous coordinates, we propose next-token diffusion, whereby a causal transformer denoises each token while attending to the clean tokens before it, without increasing context size. We train Nahual on a curated set of twelve 3D chemistry tasks ranging from microsolvation to molecular conformer search to adsorption on metal surfaces, with associated evaluation metrics and baselines. items.title: Finite temperature and pressure structural relaxations including zero-point motion and anharmonicity
items.abstract: At finite temperature and pressure, the equilibrium structure of a crystal minimizes the Gibbs free energy rather than the static Born-Oppenheimer energy. We present WARP (Wyckoff-constrained Anharmonic Relaxations at Pressure and temperature), a symmetry-constrained, variable-cell relaxation based on the stochastic temperature-dependent effective potential method, including anharmonicity and zero-point motion. Every position update is projected onto Wyckoff positions and every strain onto symmetric strains, so a relaxation can raise the symmetry but never lower it. For aluminum, the thermal expansion follows measurements at cryogenic temperatures, including the quantum plateau below 50 K. For lanthanum hydrides at megabar pressures, equations of state agree with phonon-based and path-integral calculations, and LaH$_{10}$ relaxes from its rhombohedral static minimum to the observed cubic phase, also with a machine-learned potential fine-tuned on 150 supercells. For brucite, Mg(OD)$_2$, lattice parameters, bond distances and thermal expansion agree with neutron diffraction, and the O-D isotope effect is captured.

items.title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
items.abstract: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance. Although individual numerical integration steps are inexpensive, observing meaningful events or transitions can require millions of sequential steps, resulting in substantial wall-clock simulation time and poor hardware utilization. Deep learning offers an alternative by amortizing many integration steps into a single neural network forward pass, potentially enabling much faster simulation. However, existing supervised approaches typically require long simulated trajectory data, which restricts their applicability. In this work, we introduce Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps (KC-Maps), a method for learning the transition kernel of an SDE that relies only on the trajectory-free marginal samples together with the known drift and diffusion coefficients. Given an initial time and state of a process, KC-Maps models its distribution integrated to any given time, corresponding to the weak solution of the SDE. items.title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
items.abstract: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. We introduce differentiable Equiformer fast effective-atom theory (DEFEAT), which lets a pretrained EquiformerV3 foundation model accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data, thereby enabling gradient-based materials optimization. Gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty then guide updates to composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors in a single optimization. In a search for phonon-mediated superconductors, density-functional perturbation theory on 45 structurally novel designs gives isotropic Allen-Dynes critical temperatures above 10 K for 39; the highest is 24.0 K for ZrTiNb2CN3, and H4LiPd3 (23.2 K) lies on the static DFT hull. items.title: Autonomous Optimization of Numerical Algorithms by an AI Agent: Application to Atomistic Simulation
items.abstract: Coding agents built on large language models, run in automated improvement loops, can discover more efficient algorithms. We present AIOA, a framework that brings this approach to the numerical algorithms of atomistic simulation: an agent improves an algorithm against a pre-specified metric in a loop guarded by verifiers it cannot alter. Applied to ASE, a widely used atomistic simulation library, AIOA targets two facets of an algorithm: its implementation, rewritten to run faster with unchanged results, and the method itself, redesigned to converge with fewer force evaluations. Agents made six kernels 22-24 times faster on average in Python with NumPy and SciPy. On unseen problems, optimizers from the best configuration needed 3.1-3.4 times fewer force evaluations than L-BFGS for structure relaxation and 4.6-17 times fewer than standard climbing-image nudged elastic band calculations for reaction paths. The agents' optimizers also contain two algorithmic components we did not find in the literature.

items.title: Solving Molecular Crystal Structures through Experimental PXRD-Guided Sequential Crystal Structure Prediction
items.abstract: Structure determination of organic molecular crystals relies heavily on single-crystal X-ray diffraction, yet suitable single crystals are often difficult to obtain. A common alternative uses crystal structure prediction (CSP) to generate candidate structures for subsequent comparison with experimental powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns. Such trial-and-error searches across multiple space groups incur substantial computational costs. Here, we introduce a structure determination protocol that uses experimental PXRD together with molecular structure as inputs to guide CSP from the outset. A multimodal neural network predicts probabilities for candidate space groups, which are then searched sequentially in descending probability order. Candidate structures are evaluated using PXRD agreement and relative energies, and the search terminates when a candidate satisfies the matching criterion. In a retrospective evaluation of 11 molecular-crystal systems, the protocol returned candidate sets containing structures matching the experimental crystal packing in nine cases. items.title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
items.abstract: We present a computational framework that combines machine-learning-based discovery with rigorous computer-assisted numerical certification and formal verification for strongly nonlinear partial differential equations. We demonstrate the approach for periodic gravity-capillary traveling water waves. Physics-informed neural networks are used as a search mechanism, with the wave profile, wave speed and, in continuation experiments, surface tension learned directly from the governing equations without training data. Through a staged training and refinement procedure, the neural networks achieve near-machine-precision residuals of the governing equations, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. A single formulation recovers high-amplitude Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples. Continuation from a high-amplitude Wilton ripple in surface tension reveals new high-amplitude candidate solutions. We freeze one candidate as an explicit finite representation and rigorously certify a uniform bound on its governing-equation residual using interval arithmetic, accounting for floating-point roundoff, Fourier truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors. items.title: Ab initio simulation of excited-state potential energy surfaces with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo
items.abstract: Abstract The accurate quantum chemical calculation of excited states is a challenging task, often requiring computationally demanding methods. When entire ground and excited potential energy surfaces (PESs) are desired, for instance, to predict the interaction of light excitation and structural changes, one is often forced to use cheaper computational methods at the cost of reduced accuracy. Here we introduce a method for the geometrically transferable optimization of neural network wavefunctions that leverages weight sharing and a dynamical ordering of electronic states. Our method enables the efficient prediction of ground- and excited-state PESs and their intersections at the highest accuracy, demonstrating up to two orders of magnitude cost reduction compared with single-point calculations. We validate our approach on four challenging excited-state PESs, namely, ethylene, the carbon dimer, the methylenimmonium cation and a rubredoxin active site model containing 96 electrons, illustrating the potential of transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo as a practical framework for studying electronic excitations in molecules.

rubric.why: Solid Noe-group advance in deep QMC excited states, but incremental within the neural-wavefunction line and far from MCSP needs; not landmark tier.

items.summary: Transferable neural-network wavefunction (deep QMC) optimization across geometries for excited states, via weight sharing and dynamic state ordering; claims ~100x cost reduction vs single-point runs, including conical intersections.

items.title: Variational Monte Carlo for Quantum Excited States via Nested Low-Rank Approximation
items.abstract: The electronic Schrödinger equation encodes a molecule's electronic structure and quantum properties, but solving it scales exponentially with the number of electrons. Solving this equation with neural-network variational Monte Carlo (VMC) has reached chemical accuracy on the ground state of small molecules; extending this success to excited states is constrained by two existing paradigms. Penalty-based methods need $K$ Laplacians per step but require tuning the overlap-penalty weights against the energy gaps they aim to compute. Natural excited states VMC (NES-VMC) is penalty-free, but it combines the $K$ ansatzes into one determinant, whose local energy requires $K^2$ Laplacians per step. We resolve this trade-off via low-rank approximation (LoRA) reparameterization of the rank-$K$ variational objective. The reparameterized objective admits a VMC-compatible stochastic gradient estimator via MCMC sampling from the per-state Born densities, and a sequential nesting scheme recovers the lowest $K$ eigenstates in eigenvalue order.
